learning: Iteration 8 had 60/60 finishes but about 1 line-loss event per run. Check (a) whether line_loss_events fall below 0.85 on slalom and s-bend, which would confirm the footprint causes the dropouts; (b) whether rms_error rises above 0.01 m, which would mean the wider footprint blurs the signal on sharp bends; (c) whether completion_time holds near 2.2 s on slalom; (d) whether any run goes off track. If the signal is smoother, keep sensor_size 0.016 m; if kd or kp needs retuning, the Integrator will change it next iteration.
notes: Single-variable sensing step from the iteration 8 design: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m. Controller, weights and all other geometry are unchanged so the effect on line_loss_events and rms_error can be read directly. Watch rms_error and steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom for signal blur.
rationale: Iteration 8 (score 939.3) is the best design. All 60 development trials finished, with oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20 and slalom 20/20, and rms_error of 0.0056 to 0.0099 m. The remaining score terms are line_loss_events (0.85 to 1.05 per run, up to about 15 points), completion_time (1.85 to 2.26 s) and rms_error. Iteration 8 showed that the controller has enough turn authority. The Builder's single-variable step raises sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed footprint, to keep the summed readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold on bend entries. Because the change is only in sensing, the controller should carry over unchanged, so I keep iteration 8's gains: kp 3.8, ki 0.15, kd 0.65, base_speed 1.4, the same x/0.015 sensor weights (positive = left) and last_direction line loss. Holding the controller fixed makes the sensor effect attributable. Expected result, not yet measured: line_loss_events near 0.5 to 0.85, rms_error near 0.01 m and completions at or near 60/60. The main risk is that a wider footprint blurs the signal on the sharpest bends and raises rms_error or steering_oscillation, which would show in the s-bend and slalom numbers.
